desc:
Supplier and dropship order handling makes sure every sale is sent to the right supplier and followed through to delivery. Ecom Swift LLC places orders, collects tracking numbers and adds them to your store, so customers are told.

## What is supplier order handling?

Supplier order handling is the work of passing a customer's order to the business that holds or makes the goods, and then tracking it until it arrives. It applies to dropshipping, to made-to-order products and to any store that buys from a supplier after the sale.

Some suppliers offer an automatic link with your store. Others need an email, a form or a manual order in their portal. Either way, the sequence is the same: send the order, confirm it, collect tracking, tell the customer.

## Why the link between store and supplier is fragile

Your customer only sees your store. If the supplier is late, out of stock or ships the wrong item, the customer blames you. The gap is hard to see because the information is split between two businesses, and each sale may be at a different stage.

Missed orders are the most expensive failure. A paid order that was never forwarded sits silently until the customer complains. A clear routine, with a sheet or a link that shows each order's state, prevents that.

## How a reliable supplier flow protects margin and trust

Prompt, accurate ordering shortens delivery time, which customers notice. Adding supplier tracking to your store means the shipped email carries a real link, which cuts status questions. Spotting a late or unavailable item early lets you offer a substitute or a refund before the customer asks.

There is a cost side too. Checking the price on each order against the sale price shows whether the margin held. Supplier prices change, and a product that was profitable last month may not be today.

## What a well-run supplier workflow includes

- A clear method for sending each order: automatic link or manual routine.
- An order sheet that lists each order, its supplier, its status and its cost.
- Supplier tracking numbers added to the matching store orders.
- Checks that customers receive the shipped email with a working link.
- Flags for late, backordered or out-of-stock items.
- A contact and terms sheet for each supplier.
- Rules for what to do in a stock-out or a delay.
- A margin check on cost and sale price per order.
- A written workflow your team can follow.

## What we do

We begin by learning how each supplier accepts orders and how they report tracking. Where an automatic link exists, we set it up in your account and test it. Where it does not, we create a clean manual routine and an order sheet.

Then we place the orders in your agreed batch. We check each one for the right items, variants and address, send it on, and record the confirmation. When tracking arrives we add it to the store order, and check that the customer is notified. Any order that is late or cannot be fulfilled is flagged to you quickly with options.

The Basic, Standard and Premium packages differ in the number of orders and suppliers, and in extras such as a connected supplier link, margin checks and written rules. We do not pay your suppliers on your behalf. You keep control of the supplier relationship and the payment method.

## Do and avoid

**Do:**
- Keep one sheet or system as the record of supplier orders.
- Confirm stock with the supplier before a big promotion.
- Write down each supplier's cut-off times.
- Tell customers early about any delay.
- Review supplier cost against sale price regularly.

**Avoid:**
- Forwarding orders without checking the variant and address.
- Assuming the supplier received an order that you only emailed.
- Ignoring a supplier that is repeatedly late.
- Leaving customers without tracking.
- Mixing several suppliers in one unlabelled order list.

## Who this is for

This suits a dropshipper who is spending evenings copying orders into supplier portals. It suits a maker who outsources production and needs each sale passed on in the right format. It also suits a store adding a second supplier and wanting a routine before the complexity grows.

## What we need from you

Tell us which suppliers you use and how they take orders, and share any account details through a safe method, such as a user we are invited to. We also need collaborator or staff access to your store. We never need your passwords. We reply with a checklist, then agree who approves exceptions.
